title: MLLPA — Machine Learning-assisted Lipid Phase Analysis
summary: Transformation of a lipid-membrane research method into a documented and reusable Python module combining molecular dynamics, data analysis and machine learning.

facts.label: Project type
facts.value: Python module for machine learning-assisted analysis

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Lead developer of the module, website and documentation

facts.label: Availability
facts.value: Software, website and documentation publicly available

paragraphs: The project began at the University of Strasbourg as part of research into phase transitions in lipid membranes simulated through molecular dynamics.
The work focused on lipid bilayers and their phase transitions, including the ripple phase, with a high degree of autonomy in planning the methods, stages and scientific direction.
The simulations and scientific computing workflows notably relied on GROMACS, Linux, Bash and SLURM.
I developed approximately 95% of the MLLPA code to transform the analysis methods produced during the project into a documented and reusable Python tool.

I structured the data-processing workflows and membrane-phase analyses, then developed machine-learning approaches using scikit-learn and, subsequently, a three-dimensional convolutional neural network with TensorFlow.
I also created the entire website and documentation. The work related to the 3D CNN remains unpublished and continues occasionally through collaborations.

results: Development of approximately 95% of the MLLPA module’s code.
Public availability of the software, its website and its documentation.
Publication of “A machine learning study of the two states model for lipid bilayer phase transitions” in Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics in 2020.
Publication of “MLLPA: A Machine Learning-assisted Python module to study phase-specific events in lipid membranes” in the Journal of Computational Chemistry in 2021.
Publication of “Ripple-like instability in the simulated gel phase of finite size phosphocholine bilayers” in BBA Biomembranes in 2021.
